newsitem.title: USA: US Senate unlikely to meet budget deadline-Daschle.
newsitem.headline: US Senate unlikely to meet budget deadline-Daschle.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle said lawmakers were unlikely to meet an April 15 deadline for crafting a budget resolution, the first step in the annual budgeting processs.
Speaking to reporters, Daschle said he was at a loss to understand why so little progress was underway on the budget, blaming the slowdown on Republicans.
"I don't think they are" going to meet the deadline, Daschle said. "I suspect it's still division within the Republican ranks about whether they ought to produce their own budget."
He said that until Republicans decide what they want to do, the budget process is dead in the water.

Congressional Republican leaders in recent days have called on President Clinton to resubmit his balanced budget plan, pointing to a new Congressional Budget Office analysis showing it will fall $69 billion short of balancing the budget at the end of the five-year period.
